title: Approve the draft and find the enabler in the tree
prompt:
# Story 3: Approve the draft and find the enabler in the tree

- **Story**: XXX-approve-enabler
- **Created**: 2026-11-08
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: approve a ready draft, see the message with the card that opens the file, open `architectural-enablers` in the tree, open the
  file, reload the page and find it all still there.

## Story

As a team member, I want to approve a draft so that it becomes an architectural enabler of my project and shows in the tree, so that stories
can later build on it and my team can read it.

## Acceptance tests

Approving

- [ ] **Given** a Ready draft, **Then** the card has "Discard" and "Approve and create enabler", which is enabled. **Given** any other state,
  **Then** "Approve and create enabler" is disabled.
- [ ] **Given** a Ready draft, **When** the user presses "Approve and create enabler", **Then** the enabler is stored with: id
  `0003-<slug>`, number, slug, title, the user's first prompt, today's date, the Markdown as drafted (trimmed, with one final newline), the
  links, and the ADRs it derives from.
- [ ] **Given** the Markdown, **Then** the title is read from its first `# ` line with the prefixes "Story:", "Feature specification:" and
  "AE-<digits>." taken off. **Given** it has no such line, **Then** the title is built from the first sentence of the prompt, capped at 70
  characters (cut with "..."), with the first letter in capitals.
- [ ] **Given** approval, **Then** two messages are added to the conversation: the user's prompt, and "Approved. I created architectural
  enabler AE-0003 in architectural-enablers/0003-<slug>.md. It derives from ADR 0006, ADR 0007." (with " It is linked to 2 other items." when
  there are links; "1 other item" for one), with a card showing the path and "Open file".
- [ ] **Given** approval, **Then** the draft is gone, the box is empty, the ADR chips are cleared, and the folder `architectural-enablers`
  is open in the tree.
- [ ] **Given** the user approved a second draft, **Then** its number is `0004`, even when the first words of the prompt are the same.

The tree

- [ ] **Given** an approved enabler, **Then** the folder `architectural-enablers` lists `0003-<slug>.md` in order of number, with a tooltip
  `AE-0003. <title>`, and the count of the folder is right.
- [ ] **Given** no enabler, **Then** the open folder shows the italic line "No architectural enablers yet. Write a prompt." (it showed "Coming in
  another story." before this story).
- [ ] **Given** `stories`, **Then** it stays inert, as in `story-builder-folders.md`.

Reading it

- [ ] **Given** the card in the conversation, or the file in the tree, **When** the user presses it, **Then** the file opens in the same panel
  as a driver or an ADR: icon, path, Close, the two views (rendered and Markdown), the tree as a thin rail, and the prompt as a narrow
  column on the right.
- [ ] **Given** the open enabler, **Then** it shows "Derives from" with a chip for each ADR, and, when it has links, "Linked to" with a chip for
  each. **When** the user presses a chip, **Then** that file opens.
- [ ] **Given** the open enabler, **Then** the panel says, with a lock, "Read-only here. Changing an architectural enabler comes in another
  story." and has no Save, Delete, Sync, "Add link", or "Cross enabler" control.

Discarding and keeping

- [ ] **Given** a draft is on screen, **When** the user presses "Discard", **Then** nothing is stored.
- [ ] **Given** a draft is on screen, **When** the user presses "New" in the tree header, **Then** a confirmation "Discard the draft that is
  waiting for approval?" asks first. **When** confirmed, **Then** the draft is dropped. **When** not, **Then** nothing changes.
- [ ] **Given** the "New" button, **Then** it closes any open file, shows the prompt in the middle with an empty conversation (the earlier
  messages are hidden, not deleted), puts the focus in the box, and closes the main menu to its rail.
- [ ] **Given** the page is reloaded, **Then** the approved enablers, their links and the conversation are still there. **Given** two
  projects, **Then** each keeps its own.

## Business rules and constraints

- Only a Ready draft is approved. Approving is the user's decision: the AI never stores anything.
- The identity of an enabler is its file name without ".md", `0003-<slug>`, and the reference to it is `enabler:0003-<slug>`. It comes from
  the name and never from a random id, so that a link means the same on every machine.
- The title is read from the document, so that it can be changed in the document later.
- Everything is kept in the browser in the spike (`localStorage`, per project). The final storage is another decision.
- Links to an enabler never include an ADR in `links`: the ADRs are in `derivesFrom`.

## Out of scope

- Editing the text by hand or by prompt, deleting, the *Cross enabler* flag, marking it Done or setting "Completed", and synchronising it
  with the repository, which writes `architectural-enablers/0003-<slug>.md` and `0003-<slug>.meta.json`.
- Creating the enabler without the AI, and importing enablers from the repository (they appear in the tree through the sync story).

tasks.text: Add `addEnabler` to the project store: persist the enabler record (id, number, slug, title, prompt, date, trimmed Markdown, links, derivesFrom) and the two conversation messages together in `localStorage`, keyed by project

Implement the title-extraction function: read the first `# ` line and strip the prefixes "Story:", "Feature specification:", and "AE-`<digits>`."; fall back to the first sentence of the prompt capped at 70 characters with "..."
Implement sequential number assignment across existing enablers and slug derivation from the title

Wire "Approve and create enabler" to call `addEnabler`, clear the draft, clear the prompt box and ADR chips, and open the `architectural-enablers` folder in the tree; keep the button disabled for non-Ready states
Build the approval confirmation message text (ADR list, link count) and the "Open file" card, and append both messages to the conversation

Update the `architectural-enablers` folder to list approved enablers in ascending number order with tooltips, and show the italic empty-state line "No architectural enablers yet. Write a prompt." when none exist

Implement the enabler file panel: icon, path, Close, rendered and Markdown views, "Derives from" chips, "Linked to" chips (when present), chip navigation to other files, and the locked read-only notice with no editing controls
Wire the "Open file" card and the tree file entry to open the enabler file panel

Add the "New" button to the tree header: show the confirmation dialog when a draft is present, hide earlier messages without deleting them, clear the prompt box, move focus to it, and collapse the main menu to its rail

Test: approve stores the correct record; title extraction from Markdown and from the prompt; second enabler gets number `0004`; reload restores enablers and conversation; two projects stay independent; Discard stores nothing; "New" with and without a draft in progress

Add a Flyway migration (V16, leaving the applied V15 as it is) that extends `architectural_enabler` with the title, the first prompt, the approved date, and the links and the ADRs it derives from (foreign key to the project's ADRs), and adds a `builder_message` table that keeps the conversation of each project in order (ADR-0010, ADR-0011)

Domain (`bwyn-core`): turn an approved draft into an enabler with id `0003-<slug>`; extract the title (first `# ` line without the prefixes "Story:", "Feature specification:" and "AE-`<digits>`."; else the first sentence of the prompt capped at 70 characters with "..."); trim the Markdown to one final newline; model the conversation message; extend `ArchitecturalEnablerRepository` with `save`, `findAll` and `findById` next to `nextNumber`, and add a port for the conversation (ADR-0017, AE-0005)

Application (`bwyn-application`): `ApproveArchitecturalEnablerCommand` and its handler: check that every derived ADR exists and is Accepted, assign the number (highest stored plus one when the planned one is taken), build the two messages (ADR list, link count), store the enabler and the messages in one transaction, and return what was stored (ADR-0017)
Application queries: list the enablers of a project (id, number, slug, title), read one with its Markdown, ADRs and links, and read the conversation of a project (ADR-0017)

REST (`bwyn-rest`): extend `ArchitecturalEnablersController` with the approval (POST), the list, the read of one enabler and the conversation (GET); document them with OpenAPI; answer a refusal with a status and a message the card can show (ADR-0014)
Infrastructure (`bwyn-infrastructure`): JPA entities and adapters that implement the ports, apart for each project (ADR-0011)

Replace the browser store with the backend: extend `EnablerGateway` and `HttpEnablerGateway` with approve, list, read and conversation; remove `EnablerStorage`, `BrowserEnablerStorage` and the title, Markdown, number and message-text rules now kept by the backend

Wire "Approve and create enabler" to the approval request: on success clear the draft, the prompt box and the ADR chips and open the `architectural-enablers` folder; on failure keep the draft Ready and show the error with the button available again; keep the button disabled for non-Ready states; plan the number from the backend only
Show the two messages that the backend returns, with the "Open file" card, and take the earlier messages of the session from the conversation the backend reads

Update the `architectural-enablers` folder to list the enablers the backend returns, in ascending number order with tooltips, with the italic empty-state line "No architectural enablers yet. Write a prompt." when none exist and "The architectural enablers could not be read. Try again." with a "Try again" button when they cannot be read

Wire the "Open file" card and the tree file entry to read the enabler from the backend and open the enabler file panel; when it cannot be read, open nothing and say "This file could not be read. Try again."

JUnit (domain and application): title extraction from Markdown and from the prompt, Markdown trimming, the number assigned and the next free number when the planned one is taken, the exact approval messages with and without links, the refusal of a derived ADR that is missing or not Accepted (ADR-0005, ADR-0017)

Testcontainers integration test: approve and read back the enabler and the conversation, two projects stay independent, a duplicate number is refused, a failure while storing keeps neither the enabler nor the messages, and the data is still there with a new application context (ADR-0012)

REST controller tests for the approval, the list, the read and the conversation, including the refusal; an ArchUnit rule that the new command, queries and adapters stay in their hexagonal layers (ADR-0009, ADR-0014)

Jest unit and acceptance tests: approve succeeds, approve fails and can be pressed again, the tree lists enablers read from the backend and says when it cannot, opening an enabler reads it from the backend, and enablers and conversation are still there with the browser's storage cleared; Discard sends nothing; "New" with and without a draft in progress (ADR-0005, ADR-0016)
